key_highlights: ASX dipped as oil prices jumped on US-Iran military exchanges; Middle East tensions elevate energy and risk-premium concerns
Barclays forecasts two further Fed rate hikes post-Warsh Jackson Hole speech; Australian rate expectations also rocketing
Australian home values declined sharply in August; auction sentiment deteriorating; property investor credit growth crashed post-budget tax changes
Qantas ground crews voted for possible strike action, threatening QAN.AX operations
Resource sector active: Great Southern gold drilling, Lindian rare earths, Barkly NT magnet extraction, Infini uranium, Kaiser Victorian gold
Australia flagged as risking AI economic boom due to slow uptake; Meta $24b settlement linked to social media ban
Bathla (BTL.AX) warns it could fold by week's end; Star (SGR.AX) bleeds $307m amid auditor survival doubts
One Nation commits to coal-fired power and lifting nuclear ban in Victoria; Danish firm enters to break wind farm drought

sectors.trend: Mixed. Iron ore sentiment softening ('iron ore roaches seeth'), but gold, rare earths, and uranium exploration activity is robust. Great Southern, Kaiser, Lindian, Barkly NT, and Infini advancing projects.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face headwinds from soft iron ore demand. Gold miners (GOLD.AX, NGX.AX) and rare earths/uranium names (LRE.AX, INU.AX) offer relative strength. Diversification within materials is key.

sectors.trend: Rising rate expectations support NIMs but property credit stress and investor credit crash post-budget tax changes raise NPL concerns. Macquarie (MQG.AX) $700m audit bid adds governance noise.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX benefit from higher rates but face property-sector credit risk. MQG.AX audit bid is a positive catalyst. Monitor RBA response to 'rocketing' rate expectations.

sectors.trend: Oil prices jumped on US-Iran strikes and Hormuz concerns. One Nation pushing coal and nuclear in Victoria; Danish firm entering wind. Oil giant retreating on clean energy.
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, WLE.AX, SXG.AX benefit from oil spike. Coal (BRL.AX, WES.AX) supported by One Nation policy push. Renewables (SOL.AX, LNC.AX) get Danish investment but face policy uncertainty.

sectors.trend: Woolworths (WES.AX) to stop selling Tasmanian beef; August data shows appetite for weight-loss drugs, dupe brands, and accelerating EV uptake. Qantas (QAN.AX) strike risk.
sectors.implications: WES.AX and CPL.AX face supply-chain and pricing pressure. QAN.AX faces operational disruption risk. EV and health-consumer names see tailwinds.

sectors.trend: Australia flagged as missing AI economic boom due to slow uptake. Meta $24b settlement linked to social media ban. SpaceX-AI data centre disruption discussed.
sectors.implications: ASX tech names (W1.AX, XRO.AX, BOH.AX) face structural underperformance risk. Policy action on social media could create local opportunities. AI infrastructure is a long-term theme.

sectors.trend: Home values declining sharply; auction sentiment deteriorating; property investor credit growth crashed. Bathla (BTL.AX) near collapse. Insurer cash settlements short-changing homeowners.
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX, DGL.AX) face occupancy and valuation pressure. Property developers at high distress risk. Insurance (FGP.AX, CGF.AX) under regulatory scrutiny.

key_themes: Geopolitical escalation (US-Iran, Hormuz) driving oil spike and risk-off sentiment
Global rate-hike expectations (Fed, RBA) pressuring equities and property
Australian property market in structural correction post-budget tax changes
Resource exploration renaissance: gold, rare earths, uranium, phosphate
Energy policy fragmentation: coal, nuclear, wind competing in Victoria
AI adoption gap as a structural risk for Australian productivity
Corporate distress wave: Bathla, Star, and potential insolvencies
Qantas industrial action as a consumer/transport risk

risk_assessment.risk_factor: US-Iran military escalation and Hormuz Strait disruption
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge energy exposure via WDS.AX/WLE.AX; maintain cash buffer; monitor oil above $90/bbl as escalation trigger

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Rising rate expectations (Fed + RBA) compressing valuations
risk_assessment.mitigation: Shift toward dividend-paying value (BHP.AX, CBA.AX, WES.AX); reduce duration in growth/tech; monitor RBA cash rate path

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Australian property market deterioration and credit stress
risk_assessment.mitigation: Underweight REITs and property developers; monitor bank NPL data; avoid BTL.AX and distressed property names
Reduce QAN.AX exposure pre-strike; monitor IAG.AX and travel-linked REITs for spillover

risk_assessment.risk_factor: AI adoption gap undermining Australian productivity and equity valuations
risk_assessment.mitigation: Favour ASX-listed AI infrastructure and data-centre beneficiaries; monitor government policy response
Screen small/mid-caps for going-concern risks; avoid speculative names with auditor qualification flags

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight energy producers on oil spike and Hormuz risk premium
opportunities.rationale: US-Iran strikes and Hormuz uncertainty support oil above $85; WDS and WLE benefit directly

opportunities.recommendation: Add gold and rare earths exposure as safe-haven and strategic resource plays
opportunities.rationale: Geopolitical risk supports gold; rare earths (Lindian, Barkly NT) and uranium (Infini) benefit from supply-chain diversification

opportunities.recommendation: Favour large-cap dividend payers in banks and mining for defensive income
opportunities.rationale: Higher rates support NIMs; BHP/RIO provide commodity diversification; dividend yield offsets rate-driven valuation compression

opportunities.recommendation: Monitor Victorian energy policy shift for coal/nuclear beneficiaries
opportunities.rationale: One Nation's coal and nuclear push could reshape Victorian energy mix; BRL and WES positioned

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce REIT and property developer exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Home values falling, auction sentiment weak, investor credit crashed; BTL near insolvency signals sector stress

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim QAN.AX ahead of potential ground-crew strike
defensive_moves.rationale: Strike vote passed; operational disruption risk to revenue and consumer confidence

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain 10-15% cash allocation as geopolitical and rate uncertainty persist
defensive_moves.rationale: US-Iran escalation, Fed rate-hike path, and property correction create multi-vector downside risk

defensive_moves.recommendation: Avoid small-cap speculative names with auditor or going-concern flags
defensive_moves.rationale: Star ($307m loss, auditor doubts) and Bathla (potential insolvency) signal elevated distress risk

market_outlook.short_term: ASX 200 (^AXJO) likely to remain under pressure over 1-3 months. Oil spike supports energy but rate-hike expectations and property stress weigh on financials and REITs. Qantas strike and corporate insolvencies add volatility. Expect 3-5% downside risk from current levels if Hormuz tensions escalate.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook is cautiously constructive if geopolitical tensions de-escalate. Resource exploration pipeline (gold, rare earths, uranium) supports materials sector. AI adoption gap is a structural drag but policy response could create catch-up opportunities. Property correction may stabilise by H2 2027. RBA likely to hold or cut if growth slows, supporting equities.
